stages.name: The front room
text: Telly's still warm. There's a laptop bag by the sofa and a jar of coins on the shelf that's got more in it than you'd think.
Curtains open, lights off, a games console under the telly and a handbag over the arm of a chair like it was only ever going to be borrowed.
Somebody's just moved in — boxes half-unpacked, the good stuff still in bubble wrap, a laptop charging on a pile of paperwork that has their whole life on it.
fail_text: Motion light out the back. You're over the fence before it finishes coming on.
A key turns in the front door. School run came back early and you go out the way you came in.
The telly being warm meant someone was just watching it, and someone still is, from the kitchen doorway.

stages.name: The bedroom
text: Jewellery box on the side. Watches in a bowl like they're nothing. Something's ticking somewhere and you can't find what.
Two bedside tables and only one of them's got anything in it. That tells you who's still living here, and where they keep the rings.
Bed not made, drawer half open, the whole room saying somebody left in a hurry this morning — and will come back in one too.
fail_text: Floorboard goes. Someone says 'hello?' from upstairs and you don't wait to find out who.
The jewellery box plays a tune when you open it, the kind a child would've loved and a burglar really wouldn't.
A cat you didn't know about knocks the watch bowl off the side and the whole street hears the house wake up.

stages.name: The office
text: Laptop, two phones, and a drawer that's locked, which is the only drawer in this house that's locked.
A desk with a docked laptop, a camera in a bag, and a filing cabinet somebody's put a proper lock on, which is the same as a signpost.
Home office, box of pristine tech somebody claimed back on expenses, and a hard drive that's worth nothing to you and everything to them.
fail_text: The drawer's alarmed. You've got maybe forty seconds and you spend six of them swearing.
The locked drawer's locked because it's the panic button, and you've just given it a very good reason.
A webcam light blinks on as you pass it and somewhere a phone buzzes on a nightshift worker's break.

stages.name: The safe
text: It's behind the wardrobe because of course it is. It's not a good safe. It's a safe that a man who's never been robbed thinks is a good safe.
Bolted to the floor of the airing cupboard, a keypad with four keys worn shinier than the rest — which narrows the code to about six tries.
Under the stairs, a fire safe more suited to documents than valuables, which means whatever's in it, they were more scared of losing it than of you.
fail_text: Blue light comes through the curtain. You go out the window and you leave the bag.
It's bolted through the joists and it isn't coming with you, and the drilling's brought a face to the top of the stairs.
The worn keys were a decoy code and the third wrong try triggers a dialler you can hear connecting.

stages.name: The loft
text: Nobody keeps anything up here except the things they can't explain to anyone. Which is exactly why you're going up.
The hatch is the only clean thing in a dusty house — used often, by someone hiding what they visit often, which is always worth the ladder.
Boxes labelled 'XMAS' and 'BABY' and one with no label at all, pushed to the back under the water tank where you'd put a thing you loved.
fail_text: You come down the ladder into a torch beam. That's that.
The loft boards aren't boards, they're plasterboard, and your foot comes through the landing ceiling with the rest of you close behind.
The unlabelled box is empty except for a note that says they knew this day would come, and downstairs a floorboard answers your weight.
